subject: Media Literacy
title: Platform Monopoly Power
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Platform Monopoly Power.

hook.text: When Facebook banned news in Australia, the country's access to information vanished overnight. One company, that much power.

buildup.text: A few platforms control the channels through which most people access news, information, and public discourse.

discovery.text: Platform monopolies act as gatekeepers. They decide what content is amplified, demoted, or removed entirely.

twist.text: Unlike traditional media monopolies, tech platforms claim they're neutral tools — not publishers making editorial choices.

climax.text: When a single platform can silence a president or black out an entire country's news, it wields more power than most governments.

punchline.text: The platform doesn't just host the conversation. It controls it.

quiz.question: Why is platform monopoly power concerning?
options: A few companies control how most people access news and public discourse
